evals.name: clean-up-agent-generated-comments
evals.prompt: I had Claude write this chunker for the ingestion pipeline and the comments read like a design doc. Clean them up. Leave the code alone, I only care about the comments and docstrings.
assertions: Keeps the comment '8192 is the largest input the tokenizer accepts in one call' or an equivalent statement of that constraint
Removes the plan labels 'Cluster A1' and 'Step 3'
Removes the paragraph about the rejected regex-based detector
Removes the sentence naming the indexer as the caller of is_table_start
Removes the description of split_markdown's inner loop from is_table_start's docstring
Removes the comment about normalize_headings no longer running after decoupling
Removes the reachability comment 'Callers always pass a non-empty string'
Removes the comment explaining what the caller does with the returned list
Removes the comment re-arguing the whole-file read benchmark
Removes the redundant comment '# Set the running size.'
Removes 'Takes a string and returns a list of strings' from split_markdown's docstring
Removes the words guard, canonical, idempotent, load-bearing, and downstream from all comments and docstrings
Removes the 'rows drift apart' metaphor
Rewrites the is_table_start docstring to open with a plain action rather than a noun-pile
Does not add any new comment that restates what a line of code does
Leaves the executable code unchanged

evals.name: new-code-comes-with-comments
evals.prompt: Write a Go helper for our ingestion service that reads a JSONL file of documents and returns them in batches. Batch size is capped at 4 MB because that is the request limit on the embedding endpoint we call. Skip malformed lines rather than failing the whole file, we get a few every run from a bad exporter upstream.
assertions: Comments or doc comments state why the batch cap is 4 MB, tying it to the embedding endpoint request limit
No comment restates what an adjacent line of code plainly does
No comment names a caller or describes what a consumer will do with the result
No comment discusses an alternative implementation that was not used
No comment contains the words guard, invariant, idempotent, canonical, downstream, or load-bearing
No comment carries a label from a plan or task list
The exported function's doc comment opens with the action it performs
Total comment volume is proportional to the non-obvious facts, not one comment per block

evals.name: review-a-diff-without-editing
evals.prompt: Review the comments in this file and tell me which ones you would cut and why. Don't change anything yet.
assertions: Reports findings without modifying the file
Identifies the rejected regex-based detector paragraph as removable
Identifies the plan labels Cluster A1 and Step 3 as removable
Identifies at least one comment that describes code outside the unit it sits on
Identifies the comment about code that no longer runs
Does not recommend cutting the comment about the tokenizer's 8192 input limit
Gives a reason for each finding rather than only listing line numbers
